question: Should experimental `claws update` be allowed to land with `update_partial` reporting alone, or must it first provide an operator-visible recovery/reconcile flow and live proof for external package and Gateway-cron mutations?
rationale: The implementation can fail honestly at external mutation boundaries, but deciding whether reporting partial state is an acceptable product contract versus requiring guided recovery is a maintainer safety and lifecycle-policy choice.

options.title: Require recovery and live proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until an operator-facing doctor/retry/reconcile path and redacted live evidence demonstrate package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and partial-state recovery.

options.title: Accept the experimental partial-state contract
options.body: Land behind the existing experimental gate while explicitly accepting that operators may need manual recovery after uncertain external mutations.

options.title: Pause the apply stage
options.body: Defer execution until the broader Claw lifecycle stack and RFC direction have an approved recovery model.

recommendation.title: Require recovery and live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until an operator-facing doctor/retry/reconcile path and redacted live evidence demonstrate package replacement, Gateway cron convergence, and partial-state recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review identifies the exact remaining external-boundary and recovery decision.
